title: order clerk item master uom design blank instrument
instruction:
You are Rhodri Guerrero, an order clerk supporting the integration of Aldenmere Fluid Power with the acquired hose-and-fittings businesses Birchmoor Engineering and Tanneryside Industries. The January cutover is approaching, and the operations team needs a practical decision-memo workbook that can be completed during the design review and then reused for similar item-master changes. Selma Zubair is coordinating the warehouse relabel work, Olamide Ferreira is checking the EDI implications, and the final recommendation will go to Sven Bjarnason for approval. The workbook must help the team compare the three workable approaches already under discussion: one golden SKU with an alias table, parallel SKUs mapped at order entry, and retiring the acquired numbers outright. Do not decide among those approaches for us and do not populate a sample recommendation; the point is to give the team a disciplined blank instrument in which the evidence, decision, and approval can be recorded without losing the reasoning behind it. Use the supplied file `item_master_uom_source.docx` as the sole source for the known facts, permitted vocabulary, sample source fields, and stated operating constraints. Do not add external policy, invented item numbers, or unsupported claims. Create `item_master_uom_design_memo.xlsx` in the top level of the working directory the solver starts in, using exactly that filename. It will be opened first on a laptop during the review, then printed and stapled for Sven Bjarnason's approval, so make it straightforward to navigate and usable without a training session. Keep the workbook blank in the sense that no recommendation, option selection, item records, proposed UOM conversion, score, approval outcome, initials, date, or explanatory answer may be pre-filled as an example. Labels, instructions, formulas, dropdown choices, and the source facts needed to use the instrument are allowed, but the fields where the team records its own work must remain empty until they enter it. The workbook needs an instruction or read-me area that explains the purpose, the three options, how to distinguish a source fact from an assumption and an open issue, and how the team should use the evidence and approval sections. It also needs a source-register area that lets the reviewer identify the source passage or record supporting each material claim, while preserving the source wording rather than silently rewriting it. Provide a comparison area for the three named approaches with fields for operational fit, customer impact, GTIN uniqueness, bin and legacy-WMS handling, EDI implications, cutover risk, unresolved issue, evidence reference, and reviewer comment. Include a clearly bounded recommendation and approval area in which the preparer records one selected option, the rationale, rejected alternatives and why they were set aside, assumptions, dependencies, owner, target decision date, approver, approval status, and approval comment. Include a cross-reference area for proposed item and UOM rows, with fields for acquired or legacy number, golden or parallel item identifier, description, source UOM, target UOM, conversion or packaging note, GTIN status, location or bin consequence, EDI consequence, evidence reference, and review status. The cross-reference area must support adding future rows without changing formulas or manually editing a current last-row range. The workbook should calculate useful review counts from entered rows rather than asking the user to maintain totals by hand, including counts of cross-reference rows, rows marked ready for review, rows with an unresolved issue, and rows missing an evidence reference. Put the final or boundary total in a way that is especially easy to inspect for an off-by-one error, and make that total formula-driven rather than a typed constant. Use data validation wherever the source file provides a closed vocabulary, including the option, evidence type, review status, GTIN status, and approval status fields; the dropdown values must come from a maintained list rather than being repeated as unrelated hard-coded strings. Use conditional formatting to make unresolved issues, missing evidence, and non-ready review statuses visible, but do not use colour as the only meaning. Keep all decision and cross-reference entry cells empty, keep formulas only in calculated cells, freeze a sensible navigation area, use readable number and text formats, and set print preparation so the completed memo can be printed on A4 portrait paper, fit to one page wide, with the main table headings repeated when the memo runs to additional pages. Include a small legend explaining the visual flags and a plainly labelled area for the reviewer to record whether the workbook is ready for Sven's approval. Do not include a logo, decorative stock imagery, or unrelated sections. The deliverable is the workbook only, and it must open without repair warnings in a standard offline spreadsheet application.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/item_master_uom_source.docx` — Sole source containing the supplied operating facts, the three candidate design options, permitted status and evidence vocabularies, sample source-field definitions, and constraints that the blank decision-memo instrument must support.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `item_master_uom_design_memo.xlsx` — A blank, reusable item-master and UOM cross-reference decision-memo workbook for comparing the three supplied designs, recording evidence and cross-reference rows, calculating review counts, and obtaining approval. (Place the file at the top level of the solver's starting working directory using exactly the specified filename.; Use blank_instrument polarity: all user-entered decision, item, UOM, score, approval, date, initials, and explanation fields must remain empty.; Use only the supplied DOCX as the factual source; do not invent item numbers, recommendations, policy rules, or completed examples.; The workbook must contain working formulas, maintained validation lists, conditional formatting, and expandable table structures rather than hard-coded current-row ranges.; The workbook must print on A4 portrait paper, fit one page wide, and repeat the main table headings on subsequent pages.; The workbook must open cleanly in an offline standard spreadsheet application without repair warnings.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

materials.text:
Item Master and UOM Design Review Source
Prepared for the Aldenmere Fluid Power January cutover review. This document is the sole supplied source for the decision-memo workbook.
Operating context
Aldenmere Fluid Power is integrating the acquired hose-and-fittings item masters from Birchmoor Engineering and Tanneryside Industries. The January cutover is approaching. Customers may continue quoting old part numbers on purchase orders. Case GTINs must remain unique. Bin labels and the legacy WMS cannot hold two UOMs per location. The cutover has one quiet week.
Candidate design options
One golden SKU with an alias table
Parallel SKUs mapped at order entry
Retiring the acquired numbers outright
These are the three workable approaches already under discussion; the source does not select one.
Permitted closed vocabularies
Option: One golden SKU with an alias table; Parallel SKUs mapped at order entry; Retiring the acquired numbers outright
Evidence type: Source document passage; System or master-data record; Customer or EDI record; Warehouse observation; Open issue log
Fact/assumption/open issue: Fact; Assumption; Open issue
Review status: Not started; In review; Ready for review; Blocked
GTIN status: Not checked; Unique; Concern - possible duplicate; Not applicable
Approval status: Draft; Pending approval; Approved; Returned for revision
Source-field definitions
Legacy number: Acquired or legacy number quoted or carried from a source business.
Target item identifier: Golden or parallel item identifier proposed for the target item master.
Description: Item description carried into the target record.
Source UOM: Unit of measure on the acquired or legacy record.
Target UOM: Unit of measure proposed for the target record.
Conversion or packaging note: Evidence-backed conversion, pack, or packaging detail.
GTIN status: Status of case GTIN uniqueness or checking.
Location consequence: Bin-label or location/WMS consequence.
EDI consequence: EDI mapping, order-entry, or trading-partner consequence.
Evidence reference: Short key pointing to a source passage or record in the register.
Source passages and records
P-01 | Operating context | Aldenmere Fluid Power is integrating the acquired hose-and-fittings item masters from Birchmoor Engineering and Tanneryside Industries before the January cutover.
P-02 | Customer constraint | Customers may continue quoting old part numbers on purchase orders.
P-03 | GTIN constraint | Case GTINs must remain unique.
P-04 | Warehouse constraint | Bin labels and the legacy WMS cannot hold two UOMs per location.
P-05 | Timing constraint | The cutover has one quiet week.
P-06 | Governance note | The design review compares the three candidate options and records evidence, unresolved issues, and approval; it does not prescribe a preferred option.
R-01 | Source-field record | Legacy number, target item identifier, description, source UOM, target UOM, conversion or packaging note, GTIN status, location consequence, EDI consequence, and evidence reference are the fields to carry through the cross-reference.
Classification guidance
A Fact is wording directly supported by a cited source passage or record. An Assumption is a working premise that is not yet proven by the supplied source. An Open issue is a material question or conflict that still needs an owner, evidence, or decision. Preserve the source wording in the register; do not silently rewrite it.

sheets.name: Read Me
rows: Aldenmere Item Master & UOM Design Memo
Reusable blank decision instrument | complete during design review, then print and staple for Sven Bjarnason approval
Use this blank workbook to compare the three supplied item-master designs, preserve source wording, track UOM cross-reference evidence, and prepare an approval decision for the January cutover.
1. Start in Source Register. Give each material claim a short evidence reference, select its evidence type and classification, and paste the supporting source passage or record wording unchanged.

2. In Design Options, assess every fixed option against operational fit, customer impact, GTIN uniqueness, bin/legacy-WMS handling, EDI implications, and cutover risk. Record unresolved issues, evidence references, and reviewer comments.
3. In UOM Crosswalk, add one row per acquired/legacy number and target item relationship. Use the maintained dropdowns for GTIN and review status. The table is expandable; add rows directly below it.

4. Review the calculated counts. Missing evidence, non-ready statuses, and GTIN concerns are flagged with both colour and words. Use the Approval sheet only after the evidence and trade-offs are complete.

5. On Approval, enter one selected option, rationale, rejected alternatives and reasons, assumptions, dependencies, owner, target decision date, approver, status, comment, and readiness for Sven approval. The completeness indicator is formula-driven and may show incomplete while fields are blank.

spec.professional_context: This is a wholesale item-master governance job for a small operations and delivery team. The finished workbook is a reusable decision-memo instrument that can be completed by an order clerk and approved by operations leadership before a WMS and EDI cutover.
difficulty_sources: Choosing and documenting a defensible cross-reference design under competing operational constraints
Separating source facts, assumptions, open decisions, and approval evidence
Building a reusable blank workbook whose formulas, dropdowns, and ranges continue to work as rows are added

content_requirements: State that Aldenmere Fluid Power is integrating an acquired hose-and-fittings item master before a January cutover.
Describe the three candidate options exactly as: one golden SKU with an alias table; parallel SKUs mapped at order entry; retiring the acquired numbers outright.

State the constraints: customers may continue quoting old part numbers on purchase orders; case GTINs must remain unique; bin labels and the legacy WMS cannot hold two UOMs per location; the cutover has one quiet week.
Provide closed vocabularies for option, evidence type, review status, GTIN status, and approval status.

Provide source-field definitions for legacy number, target item identifier, description, source UOM, target UOM, conversion or packaging note, GTIN status, location consequence, EDI consequence, and evidence reference.
Include several internally consistent sample source records or passages so the instrument can support evidence referencing without requiring live data.
Explicitly distinguish facts, assumptions, and open issues.

required: Definitions of source fact, assumption, and open issue
Descriptions of the three candidate options
Instructions for evidence references, review counts, and approval

rules: Evidence reference and source passage fields are blank input fields.
Evidence type and fact/assumption/open-issue fields use validation lists derived from the source.
The three option labels are present as fixed row labels, but all assessment, evidence, issue, and comment fields are blank.
Include a formula-driven review-summary area that counts option rows with evidence references and unresolved issues using structured table references.
Include a boundary total or final summary cell whose formula covers the full expandable option table and is not a typed constant.
Use an Excel Table or equivalent expandable structured range so formulas and validation apply to added rows without editing a today-only row range.
Provide formula-driven counts for total entered rows, ready-for-review rows, unresolved or non-ready rows, and rows missing evidence.
The count formulas must use table or dynamic-range logic and must not depend on a fixed last row.
GTIN status and review status use source-derived dropdown lists.
Conditional formatting flags missing evidence, unresolved/non-ready status, and GTIN concerns with text labels or equivalent non-colour cues.
Selected option and approval status use source-derived validation lists.
Ready-for-approval is a blank user-entry or formula-supported review field, but must not contain a completed answer.
Include a formula-driven completeness indicator that identifies missing evidence or missing required approval fields without supplying their values.

global_affordances: Use workbook-level maintained validation lists, preferably on a hidden or clearly separated list area, and have dropdowns reference those lists.
Use formulas for every calculated count and boundary total.
Freeze panes appropriate to each working sheet.
Set A4 portrait, fit-to-width one page, repeat main table headings, and define print areas that include the relevant instructions or legend.
Protect or visually distinguish formula cells from blank entry cells without preventing ordinary completion.
Do not include logos, images, decorative examples, or prefilled answer content.

authoring_plan.gold_derivation: Build the source DOCX first, then construct the workbook with the schema above. Inspect the XLSX with openpyxl to verify sheet order, tables, formulas, data validations, conditional formatting, freeze panes, number formats, print settings, print titles, and blank entry cells. Add rows to the crosswalk table in a test copy and confirm formulas, validation, and counts continue to cover the added rows. Render or print-preview the workbook with an available offline office tool or inspect page setup XML where rendering is unavailable. The gold should pass every rubric item without relying on a completed recommendation.

reference_files.purpose: Sole source containing the supplied operating facts, the three candidate design options, permitted status and evidence vocabularies, sample source-field definitions, and constraints that the blank decision-memo instrument must support.
reference_files.discovery: Read this file before constructing the workbook; it is the only supplied source and must be cited by the workbook's source-register affordance.

deliverables.description: A blank, reusable item-master and UOM cross-reference decision-memo workbook for comparing the three supplied designs, recording evidence and cross-reference rows, calculating review counts, and obtaining approval.
constraints: Place the file at the top level of the solver's starting working directory using exactly the specified filename.
Use blank_instrument polarity: all user-entered decision, item, UOM, score, approval, date, initials, and explanation fields must remain empty.
Use only the supplied DOCX as the factual source; do not invent item numbers, recommendations, policy rules, or completed examples.
The workbook must contain working formulas, maintained validation lists, conditional formatting, and expandable table structures rather than hard-coded current-row ranges.
The workbook must print on A4 portrait paper, fit one page wide, and repeat the main table headings on subsequent pages.
The workbook must open cleanly in an offline standard spreadsheet application without repair warnings.
